summary: Frontend-only retest of webpackPrefetch magic comment on the AmbientHeat lazy import. VERIFIED: <link rel=prefetch> for the AmbientHeat chunk is emitted in the DOM at ~662ms after cold nav (found href=/static/js/src_components_AmbientHeat_jsx.chunk.js). The prefetch fires the chunk request very early — network log shows the AmbientHeat chunk request at t=-37ms (right at/before navigationStart baseline) plus follow-ups at 535/549ms. All iter5 regression checks still pass: hero-fallback paints early, three blooms present and animating, timelapse-stamp still shows '◉ timelapse · <date> <hour>h UTC · frame N/43', localStorage cache 'pulse:timelapse:v1' still written, window.__PULSE_TIMELAPSE_PROMISE__ still 'object' after paint, /map and /trending routes still function. HOWEVER — measured paint times were WORSE than iter5's baseline on this run (cold 23.5s vs 14.0s; cache-hit 10.9s vs 7.6s). This is almost certainly preview-host variance (the code path once the chunk arrives is identical to iter5), but the improvement direction for prefetch cannot be confirmed from a single sample.

integration_issues.issue: Cold time-to-timelapse-stamp measured 23564ms and cache-hit 10866ms — both slower than iter5's baselines (14.0s cold / 7.6s cache-hit). The prefetch link IS emitted correctly and the chunk request DOES fire earlier (network log shows AmbientHeat chunk requested near t=0ms), so this regression is very likely preview-tunnel/CRA-dev-server variance rather than the webpackPrefetch change causing harm. Recommend recording ~3 samples per condition to smooth noise before drawing conclusions. Functionally everything is fine.

critical_code_review_comments: webpackPrefetch magic comment placement is correct — inside import() as the first arg comment, and CRA/webpack correctly emits the <link rel=prefetch> tag pointing at the emitted chunk.

Prefetch fires the chunk request at essentially t=0 relative to nav (network log: -37ms), which is the intended behavior. This closes the gap of ~200-500ms that iter5 had between main-bundle parse and lazy-chunk fetch initiation. Whether that translates to a visible paint-time win depends on host consistency.
